metadata.title: Random But True: The Monster One Guy Built In A Single Forum Post
metadata.caption:
On June 10, 2009, a Something Awful forum user named Eric Knudsen - posting as "Victor Surge" - entered a Photoshop contest. The challenge: fake a paranormal photo.

He added a tall, faceless figure in a black suit to two ordinary black-and-white photos of kids playing, wrote a few lines of fake witness testimony, and named it the Slender Man. That's the entire origin. No ancient legend, no case file. One forum post.

Then the internet did the rest. Other users built him a fake past - including a supposed 16th-century German woodcut nicknamed "Der Großmann" - specifically designed to make him look like folklore that predates the internet by centuries. None of it was real.

It worked. Video games, a feature film, and a found-footage web series (Marble Hornets) followed - and millions of people genuinely couldn't tell where the hoax ended.

In 2014, two 12-year-old girls in Waukesha, Wisconsin stabbed a classmate in the woods, telling police they did it to please Slender Man. She survived. Both girls were later found not guilty by reason of mental illness and committed to psychiatric institutions.

Eric Knudsen gave a statement afterward: "I am deeply saddened by the tragedy in Waukesha, Wisconsin. My thoughts are with the family of the victim..."
